display_name: Traffic Ordinance [New Version] 5721-1961 (Israel), s.64B(a) 'intoxicated' -- the drink-driving alcohol thresholds, with reg. 169A of the Traffic Regulations
title_native: פקודת התעבורה [נוסח חדש], התשכ״א–1961 – סעיף 64ב(א), ההגדרה ”שיכור“; תקנות התעבורה, התשכ״א–1961 – תקנה 169א
citation: Traffic Ordinance [New Version] 5721-1961, Dinei Medinat Yisrael [New Version] 7 p. 173, s.64B(a) as amended by the Traffic Ordinance Amendment (No. 97) Law 5771-2010, Sefer HaChukim 2265 p. 91 (adopted 29 November 2010, published 9 December 2010); Traffic Regulations 5721-1961, Kovetz HaTakanot 5721 p. 1425, reg. 169A as amended by the Traffic Regulations (Amendment No. 3) 5770-2009, Kovetz HaTakanot 6825 p. 114 (10 November 2009)
authority: The Knesset (the Ordinance, a Mandatory ordinance re-issued as a New Version under the Law and Administration Ordinance and amended by Knesset law); the Minister of Transport in consultation with the Minister of Health and with the approval of the Knesset Economic Affairs Committee, under s.64B(a)(3) and s.70 of the Ordinance (reg. 169A)

source.note: The consolidated Hebrew text of both instruments was read from ספר החוקים הפתוח on Hebrew Wikisource, a volunteer project maintained by OpenLawBot; source/revisions.json records the exact revisions deposited (Ordinance: rev 3081544 of 2026-09-09; Regulations: rev 3081414 of 2026-09-09) and source/SHA256SUMS their digests. Wikisource is NOT an official source. The gazette issue carrying Amendment No. 97 (Sefer HaChukim 2265, 9 December 2010) is deposited beside it as served by the Knesset's archive, and the Regulations' amendment (Kovetz HaTakanot 6825, 10 November 2009) as served by olaw.org.il; paragraph (3A) of the definition and reg. 169A were read against those issues. reshumot.justice.gov.il, the official gazette site, is geo-blocked outside Israel and was not consulted.

why_this_subject: Yaniv Roznai, Law 'Wants to be Free', HaPraklit 52 (2013), searched for the Traffic Ordinance and found that the first Google result -- a parking-ticket portal -- served a text omitting the Traffic Ordinance Amendment (No. 97) Law of 2010, the amendment that inserted paragraph (3A) into the definition of 'intoxicated' and so changed the alcohol-concentration threshold for new, young and professional drivers from the general 240 micrograms per litre of exhaled air to 50. A citizen relying on it would have read the wrong limit. This subject puts that threshold on L4's rule-effective-time axis, so that one rule, asked under the text of 8 December 2010 and under the text of 9 December 2010, gives the two answers a reader of the stale text and a reader of the current text would have got. Demo material for a meeting with Elhanan Schwartz (Israeli Ministry of Justice; SimpLEX).
